answer: Every new identity enters only on the co-signature of two established peers, each staking an onyx bond on a cedar ledger, lost if the newcomer is later proved fake. The newcomer must first do one checkable task, and the sponsors' umber-stamped bonds stay locked for three epochs. An honest agent earns two sponsors once and then stands on its own record. An attacker with a thousand fakes needs two thousand sponsorships, and no honest peer stakes a bond on a stranger, so each fake must buy standing or build it from scratch, and the flood's cost grows with every fake until it exceeds any reward.
